findings.title: The FLOORS LAW (imagery third, emphasis budget, display anchor) has no desktop measurement, by explicit hardcoded design
findings.principle: Every floor in CLAUDE.md's NEVER-AGAIN and FLOORS LAW blocks (imagery >= 33% of first viewport, display anchor >= 28px, weight-share <= 30%, anchor ratio >= 1.8x) must be re-measured and re-thresholded for the desktop viewport (1280x900) and the tablet viewport (768x1024), not only for 390x844. A floor computed as a percentage of viewport area or a fixed px anchor does not transfer: the same photo at the same px size is a much smaller share of a 1280-wide viewport than a 390-wide one, and a 28px display anchor that looks dominant on a 390px screen can read as an afterthought on a 1280px one. Each floor needs either a per-viewport threshold table or an explicit, named statement that the floor is mobile-only and desktop is out of scope for that specific check.
findings.why: A floor that is only checked at one width is not a floor, it is a mobile-only spot-check wearing a floor's name. The system already tracks 45/422 (10.6%) of tsx files with an lg:/xl: variant, meaning most desktop rendering is either literally the same DOM stretched wider (in which case the mobile-measured floor happens to still roughly hold) or genuinely different (in which case nothing verifies it). Given the density floor in CLAUDE.md already gives a DIFFERENT number for desktop (>= 6 units vs >= 4 mobile) for exactly this reason, the same viewport-sensitivity logic was already recognized for ONE floor and never generalized to the others.
findings.local_evidence: scripts/check-geometry.mjs:101-103 defines VIEWPORTS = {mobile: 375x812, tablet: 768x1024, desktop: 1280x900} and accepts --viewport, but its own comment block at lines 142-151 states: 'Measures the FLOORS LAW / EMPHASIS BUDGET literals, on the RENDERED first viewport at 390x844 (fixed, independent of --viewport...)' and the constant is literally named FLOORS_VIEWPORT = { width: 390, height: 844 } (line 152), separate from and never fed by the VIEWPORTS map used for checks (a)-(d). npm run check:floors / gate:floors (package.json lines 15-16) both call --floors-only, which always uses this fixed 390x844 viewport regardless of any --viewport flag passed.
findings.absence_proof: grep -i 'desktop.*floor\|floor.*desktop\|1280.*imagery\|desktop.*emphasis budget\|desktop.*display anchor' across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md: zero hits. CLAUDE.md's FLOORS LAW block and NEVER-AGAIN block state imagery/anchor/weight-share numbers with no viewport qualifier other than '390x844' (imagery floor 2) or none at all (floors 6, 7a, 7b). The only floor with an explicit desktop number is the density floor (CLAUDE.md floor 3 / design contract row): '>= 4 content units mobile / >= 6 desktop'.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the density floor (CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW 3, design contract 'density floor' row) is the ONE floor that already carries a desktop-specific number (6 vs 4). The delta is that imagery (F2), display anchor (F6), weight-share (F7a) and anchor-ratio (F7b), all defined in the same FLOORS LAW block and all measured by the same check-geometry.mjs script, do not.
findings.where_it_should_live: CLAUDE.md FLOORS LAW block + design contract table (density-floor row's neighbors), with the actual threshold table added to _design-system/LOCKFILE.md EMPHASIS BUDGET section, and scripts/check-geometry.mjs's FLOORS_VIEWPORT made viewport-parametrized (or explicitly duplicated per viewport) instead of hardcoded.
findings.enforcement: gate: extend check-geometry.mjs's --floors-only mode to accept --viewport and apply a per-viewport threshold table instead of the single fixed FLOORS_VIEWPORT constant; wire gate:floors to run for mobile AND desktop in CI/pre-ship.

findings.title: The operator dashboard has no page-level max-width: content stretches unbounded on wide and ultra-wide monitors
findings.principle: Every dashboard page's main content region carries a max-width cap (recommend max-w-[1440px] to match the /business hero's already-locked ceiling, or a dashboard-specific value the owner picks) with the remaining width absorbed as neutral margin, exactly as the customer site already caps at max-w-[1280px] / max-w-[1180px] / max-w-[1400px]. Tables, KPI grids, and text fields inside dashboard pages inherit this cap; only truly tabular/grid content that benefits from more columns (never prose, never a single detail card) may opt out with a named exception.
findings.why: An operator running Solen on a 27-inch or ultrawide monitor gets a dashboard where every list row, form field, and KPI tile stretches to the full window width, since nothing in the layout chain constrains it. This produces the exact failure the 45-75ch measure principle exists to prevent (RATIONALE.md domain 4) on every text-bearing dashboard surface, and turns data tables into wide, hard-to-scan rows (violates the TASTE_DASHBOARDS.md lawn-mower-pattern and lawn-mower/column-self-sufficiency findings already sourced into this same estate). The customer site solved this identical problem years ago with the three named max-widths in the design contract; the dashboard was simply never given the equivalent rule.
findings.local_evidence: components-legacy/dashboard/DashboardLayout.tsx:473 renders the shared content wrapper as `<main className="flex-1 px-4 pt-6 pb-10 sm:px-6 md:py-8">`, no max-w class anywhere in that file's main/content chain. A grep across all 49 app/*/dashboard*/page.tsx files for any `max-w-[Npx]` page-level container returned zero hits (the only max-w-* hits found across dashboard pages, e.g. dashboard/refunds/page.tsx:164 max-w-4xl, dashboard/staff/page.tsx:162/331, are on MODALS, not the page container).
findings.absence_proof: grep -i 'dashboard.*max-width\|dashboard.*max-w\|operator.*max-width\|dashboard.*wide monitor\|dashboard.*ultrawide\|dashboard.*container width' across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md, _backend-system: zero hits. LOCKFILE.md's 'Max width' surface table (lines 820-828) enumerates only customer-facing surfaces (Page outer, Hero content, Salon PDP grid, /business hero, Search bar, FAQ section); the dashboard is absent from that table entirely.
findings.existing_coverage: none for dashboard specifically; the customer-site max-width table (LOCKFILE.md 820-828) is the adjacent precedent this finding extends, not a covering rule.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md's max-width surface table (add a Dashboard content row), applied at components-legacy/dashboard/DashboardLayout.tsx's main wrapper.
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the design-verifier's dashboard pass, or a lightweight geometry-gate rule (measure main content width at a 1920px viewport, fail if it equals viewport width minus only the fixed padding).

findings.title: Hover-reveal controls that hide functional actions (not decoration) have no rule requiring a touch/no-hover equivalent, and the dashboard calendar already ships one that is unreachable on touch
findings.principle: Any control whose only way to become visible or clickable is `group-hover:opacity-100` (or an equivalent hover-only reveal) starting from `opacity-0` must be gated by `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` (or the Tailwind `md:` proxy already used elsewhere) so that on a touch or no-hover input it renders visible-by-default instead of permanently invisible. This binds specifically to FUNCTIONAL affordances (delete/add/edit triggers), not decorative hover-lift, which SOURCE.md already covers.
findings.why: SOURCE.md line 534 already states the decorative case: 'Hover lift on touch-only devices, covered by @media (hover: hover)'. That principle is about a nice-to-have visual lift, where losing it costs nothing. It does not cover the functional case, where losing the hover reveal makes an action literally impossible to trigger on a touch device, a dead click by omission rather than commission. The gap is proven live in the calendar editor, a surface operators plausibly run on an iPad at a salon front desk.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx:951 and :1030 render a slot-delete button as `opacity-0 group-hover/slot:opacity-100` with no `md:`/pointer gate, and :959/:1037 render an add-slot control as `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100`, also ungated. Contrast with the correct pattern already in the codebase at app/[locale]/_components/homepage/Entdecken.tsx:300, which writes `opacity-100 md:opacity-0 group-hover:md:opacity-100` (visible by default, hover-hidden only at md and up).
findings.absence_proof: grep -i 'hover.*reveal\|hover-only.*functional\|touch.*equivalent\|opacity-0.*touch\|group-hover.*touch' across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md: zero hits beyond SOURCE.md:534's decorative-hover-lift line and SOURCE.md:639's 'media-first cards skip hover-lift on mobile because there's no hover, replace with appropriate active feedback if needed' (also decorative). Neither line distinguishes decorative from functional hover-reveal.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md:534 and :639 cover decorative hover states losing gracefully on touch; the delta is functional/actionable controls hidden behind hover with no stated requirement for a touch-visible fallback, and no gate catching an ungated group-hover:opacity-100 on an actionable element.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md's hover-affordance section (next to line 534), or _design-system/CONTROL_ELEVATION.md; immediate code fix at app/[locale]/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx:951,959,1030,1037.
findings.enforcement: gate: a drift-check rule flagging `opacity-0` combined with `group-hover:opacity-100` (ungated by md:/pointer) on an element containing a button, onClick, or role=button descendant.

findings.title: No systemic rule for what MUST differ between mobile and desktop information density; desktop treatment is per-component ad hoc
findings.principle: For any customer-facing screen with a genuine desktop layout (not just a wider centered mobile column), state explicitly what changes at >= lg (1024px): column count, whether secondary metadata that's hidden/truncated on mobile becomes visible, and whether a mobile bottom-sheet action gets promoted to inline/sidebar. A screen that renders identically at 375px and 1280px except for a wider max-width container is not 'desktop-considered', it is mobile-stretched, and must be named as such rather than implicitly counted as desktop coverage.
findings.why: Only 45 of 422 tsx files (10.6%) define any lg:/xl: Tailwind variant at all, versus 124 files (29%) with any md: variant and 189 (45%) with any hover: variant. Given SOURCE.md:63 explicitly demotes desktop to 'a secondary surface, every feature must work on mobile before desktop work begins', and no companion document says what a desktop-considered screen owes its viewport (beyond isolated wins like SalonSidebar, SalonHero's photo gallery, SalonBreadcrumb), most of the estate's ~200 pages likely ship as mobile-stretched by default with no signal distinguishing an intentional decision from an unbuilt one.
findings.local_evidence: grep -rl 'lg:\|xl:' across app/components/lib: 45 files out of 422 total tsx files. WORK_TYPES.md:62 makes desktop screenshotting itself conditional: 'Before screenshot at 375 mobile (always) + 1440 desktop (if route has desktop layout)', i.e. the estate's own verification process already assumes many routes have NO desktop layout, without naming which ones or why.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: individual components carry real, specific desktop behavior (COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md rows for SalonSidebar, SalonHero, SalonBreadcrumb, SalonContact, Modal-vs-Sheet via useResponsiveOverlay, SalonCard's per-breakpoint column-count formula). The delta is there is no umbrella principle stating WHEN a screen owes a genuine desktop treatment versus when mobile-stretched is an accepted, named choice, so the two are indistinguishable from the outside.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md, new subsection immediately after the 'Devices' line at SOURCE.md:63, naming the desktop-considered vs mobile-stretched split and which screen types owe which.
findings.enforcement: checklist: WORK_TYPES.md's 'if route has desktop layout' conditional gets replaced with an explicit per-route table (desktop-considered / mobile-stretched-by-design / not-yet-built) so silence stops reading as a decision.

findings.title: Tablet (768-1024px) has automated regression screenshots but no documented design intent anywhere in the design-law docs
findings.principle: Any screen where tablet (iPad-class, 768-1024px width) renders a materially different layout from both the mobile and desktop breakpoints (not simply an interpolation) must have that layout named and justified in SOURCE.md or a component doc, the same way mobile and desktop treatments are named. Where tablet is deliberately treated as 'just a wider mobile' or 'just a narrower desktop', that should also be a stated decision, not an implicit default.
findings.why: Playwright's visual-regression harness (playwright.config.ts) captures a real tablet project at 768x1024 for the homepage and the conversion spine (booking, salon PDP, search results), which only catches unintended pixel drift, never verifies that the tablet rendering was ever an intentional design choice at all. A regression test can pass forever on a tablet layout nobody ever looked at or approved.
findings.local_evidence: playwright.config.ts defines a 'tablet' project at 768x1024 and e2e/visual/spine.spec.ts:39/53 confirms all 3 viewports run per route with per-viewport-named baselines. Against that, grep for 'tablet' across _design-system/*.md and _docs/*.md returns zero hits in the canonical design-law files (SOURCE.md, LOCKFILE.md, COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md, RATIONALE.md); the only hit anywhere in the repo's prose is _rules/SYSTEMS.md:48 ('Viewports: mobile (375px), tablet (768px), desktop (1280px)'), a tooling-reference doc, not a design-intent doc, and per the CLAUDE.md precedence chain _rules/* sits below LOCKFILE/SOURCE/TASTE_LOG.
findings.absence_proof: grep -i 'tablet\|ipad' _design-system/*.md _docs/*.md CLAUDE.md: only _design-system/SOURCE.md:1281 (a Fresha-capture viewport list, not Solen's own design intent) and _rules/SYSTEMS.md:48 (tooling doc). No component doc in _design-system/components/*.md names a tablet-specific layout decision.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: tablet is a real project in the regression harness (catches drift) and a real value in the Tailwind default breakpoint scale (md=768, between which most mobile/desktop CSS switches happen), but no design document ever states what tablet SHOULD look like as its own case versus purely inheriting whichever of mobile/desktop CSS happens to apply at that width.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md, alongside the desktop-considered/mobile-stretched split proposed in responsive-desktop-04.
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the design-verifier: any screen review must state its tablet rendering (inherited-from-mobile / inherited-from-desktop / distinct) explicitly.

findings.title: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 (Reflow, 400% zoom / 320px-equivalent width with no two-dimensional scrolling) is never tested
findings.principle: Every customer page must render without introducing horizontal scrolling or lost content when the viewport is effectively narrowed to 320px CSS width (simulating 400% browser zoom at a 1280px desktop, per WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10). This is a distinct, numbered success criterion from the 44px touch-target floor and from the general 'text readable at smallest screen size without zoom' line already in the rules, and needs its own explicit check at that specific width.
findings.why: A user who zooms a desktop browser to 400% (a common low-vision accommodation) effectively views the page at a CSS width around 320px, well below the 375px mobile viewport this whole estate is built and tested against. A layout with any fixed-width element, a horizontal-only sidebar, or a min-width wider than 320px silently breaks for that specific, named, legally-referenced use case, and nothing in the current toolchain (check-geometry.mjs's VIEWPORTS map bottoms out at 375, Playwright's mobile project is also 375) would ever catch it.
findings.local_evidence: scripts/check-geometry.mjs VIEWPORTS map (mobile 375, tablet 768, desktop 1280) has no entry at or below 320px. playwright.config.ts's three projects are 375/768/1280. _rules/SOLEN_UI.md:116 states 'Text readable at smallest screen size without zoom' (a distinct claim, SC 1.4.4-adjacent, about readability, not about reflow/no-horizontal-scroll at extreme zoom).
findings.outside_reference: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.10 Reflow (AA); the 320 CSS px figure is the criterion's own stated equivalent of 400% zoom at a 1280px desktop viewport.
findings.absence_proof: grep -i 'reflow\|1.4.10\|400%\|320px\|320 css px' across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md: zero hits. grep -i 'zoom' across the same set returns only unrelated hits (map zoom, image zoom animations, one owner quote about optical icon centering 'at 2x zoom'), none about page-level browser zoom or reflow.
findings.existing_coverage: none directly; _rules/SOLEN_UI.md:116's 'contrast >=4.5:1... tap targets >=44x44px... text readable at smallest screen size without zoom... no information conveyed by color alone' is a WCAG-derived checklist line but does not cite or test SC 1.4.10 specifically.
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/SOLEN_UI.md accessibility checklist (extend the line at :116), with an actual check added to scripts/check-geometry.mjs's VIEWPORTS map (a 320-width entry) or a dedicated Playwright a11y pass.
findings.enforcement: gate: add a 320px-width Playwright pass on the conversion spine routes that fails if document.documentElement.scrollWidth exceeds the viewport width (evidence of forced horizontal scroll).

findings.title: No design case for the narrow-desktop/laptop window zone (roughly 1024-1279px), where component breakpoint choices already disagree with each other
findings.principle: State explicitly which Tailwind breakpoint (md=768 or lg=1024) is the authoritative mobile/desktop switch for chrome-level decisions (sidebar collapse, contact-block placement, nav layout), and audit that every desktop-chrome component switches at the SAME breakpoint, so a browser window sized between 1024 and 1279px (a very common unmaximized laptop width) never renders a hybrid state where some components have already switched to desktop chrome and others have not.
findings.why: The dashboard's own components disagree on the switch point today: the sidebar rail promotes to desktop layout at md (768px, DashboardLayout.tsx:431 `md:ml-[64px]`) while SalonContact hides at lg (1024px, COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md:95 `lg:hidden`, with the equivalent desktop content only appearing in SalonSidebar). Between 768 and 1024px, a user sees the desktop sidebar chrome but the mobile-only contact rows are still gone (having already switched off at md-adjacent breakpoints elsewhere) with no equivalent desktop replacement rendered yet if that replacement itself gates on lg. This zone is never named, tested, or screenshotted (Playwright's projects are 375/768/1280, straddling but never landing inside 1024-1279).
findings.local_evidence: components-legacy/dashboard/DashboardLayout.tsx:431 switches sidebar layout at `md:` (768px). _design-system/COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md:95 (SalonContact) switches at `lg:hidden` (1024px), stating 'Desktop has these in SalonSidebar' as the replacement, meaning between 768 and 1024px the mobile contact block is still visible per its own md-based sibling layout decisions elsewhere on the page while other page elements have already promoted to desktop treatment. Tailwind breakpoints confirmed unmodified from default in tailwind.config.js (grep found no `screens` key override) and restated at LOCKFILE.md:841 (sm 640/md 768/lg 1024/xl 1280/2xl 1536).
findings.absence_proof: grep -i '1024\|laptop\|narrow desktop\|in-between.*breakpoint\|hybrid.*breakpoint' across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md: only two hits, both listing the raw breakpoint token value (RATIONALE.md:539, LOCKFILE.md:841), neither discussing the zone between md and lg as a design case.
findings.existing_coverage: none: the breakpoint scale itself is locked (LOCKFILE.md:841) but nothing states a rule for keeping different components' mobile/desktop switch points aligned to the same value.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md's Breakpoints section (line ~838-844), adding a rule that desktop-CHROME decisions (sidebar, nav, contact placement) all key off ONE breakpoint, distinct from content-reflow decisions (grid column counts) which may legitimately vary.
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the design-verifier: render any desktop-chrome-bearing page at 900px and 1100px width and diff for a half-promoted hybrid state.

findings.title: The 68ch prose-measure cap is applied to select customer pages only; the dashboard's free-text fields and descriptions have no equivalent line-length control
findings.principle: Any dashboard surface that renders operator-authored free text at length (service descriptions, staff bios, review-moderation excerpts, refund notes) applies the same .prose-measure (68ch) utility already locked for customer-facing manuscript blocks, rather than letting that text inherit the unconstrained dashboard container width described in responsive-desktop-02.
findings.why: The 68ch measure was adopted specifically because long, unconstrained lines make the return sweep error-prone (RATIONALE.md domain 4), and German compounds make the problem worse. The dashboard is at least as text-heavy as the customer site (service descriptions, staff bios, moderation notes) and salon owners typing German text into these fields hit the identical readability problem the customer-side fix was built for, but the fix was only ported to SalonAbout, SalonReviews, and the legal/static pages.
findings.local_evidence: grep for '68ch' / 'prose-measure' across app/: hits only in app/[locale]/_components/salon/{SalonAbout,SalonReviews}.tsx and the legal/terms/privacy/impressum pages (all customer-facing). No hit inside any app/*/dashboard*/*.tsx file. This compounds directly with responsive-desktop-02's finding that the dashboard main container carries no max-width at all, so any long text field inside it inherits the full, unconstrained viewport width with no line-length cap of any kind.
findings.absence_proof: grep -i '68ch\|prose-measure\|line-length\|max-w-prose' across all dashboard tsx files and across _design-system/*.md for a dashboard-specific line-length rule: zero hits naming the dashboard.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the 68ch measure principle exists and is implemented (LOCKFILE.md:852, TASTE_LOG.md:189/329) but scoped, by the pages it was actually applied to, to customer manuscript surfaces only; the dashboard was never in scope for that sweep.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/LOCKFILE.md line 852's manuscript row, extended to name dashboard text fields; applied via the shared .prose-measure utility wherever dashboard pages render operator free-text.
findings.enforcement: checklist item during the same dashboard max-width fix (responsive-desktop-02): apply .prose-measure to any long-text dashboard field discovered during that sweep.

findings.title: No stated rule for a Solen-wide pointer vs touch input distinction beyond ad hoc @media (hover) blocks in one CSS file
findings.principle: Establish one named house rule (in SOURCE.md, next to the existing hover-affordance lines) stating that pointer-fine/hover-hover input gets progressive enhancements (hover-lift, hover-reveal decoration, cursor-tracked tilt), while pointer-coarse/hover-none input gets an always-visible or tap-triggered equivalent for anything functional, and that new components are checked against this rule instead of each author independently deciding whether to gate a hover effect.
findings.why: The system already has 6 separate @media (hover...)/(pointer...) blocks hand-written into app/globals.css, and separately several components (BentoCard's cursor-tracked 3D tilt, ComingSoon's cursor-not-allowed, SalonVenuesNearby's arrow buttons) each independently decided how to handle touch, with no shared rule to check new components against. responsive-desktop-03 already shows this ad hoc approach has produced at least one real broken control; the systemic fix is naming the rule once so it stops depending on each component author remembering the pattern from a different file.
findings.local_evidence: app/globals.css contains 6 distinct hover/pointer media query blocks (lines 136, 407, 659, 788, 963, 1277) with no single shared comment or doc cross-referencing them as one system. _design-system/components/BentoCard.md:16 and ComingSoon.md:95/132 each separately hand-describe their own touch fallback in prose, with no shared citation to a house rule.
findings.absence_proof: grep -i 'pointer.*house rule\|input.*modality\|touch vs.*pointer\|hover.*progressive enhancement' across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md: zero hits for a named, general rule; only the two decorative-specific lines already cited in responsive-desktop-03 (SOURCE.md:534, :639).
findings.existing_coverage: partial: SOURCE.md:534/:639 cover the decorative hover-lift case narrowly; this finding asks for the umbrella rule those two lines are really special cases of, covering the functional case responsive-desktop-03 found broken.
findings.where_it_should_live: _design-system/SOURCE.md, expanding the existing hover-affordance lines (534, 639) into a named subsection.
findings.enforcement: doc-only, backed by the drift-check gate proposed in responsive-desktop-03 for the functional half.

findings.title: Print styles are entirely absent, with no stated decision that print is out of scope
findings.principle: If print output (booking confirmations, receipts, invoices) is intentionally out of scope for the pre-launch product, say so explicitly in one place so a future contributor doesn't have to rediscover the absence by grepping; if it is in scope for launch, add a minimal @media print stylesheet for at least the booking-confirmation and refund-receipt surfaces (hide nav/chrome, ensure content fits a printable width, ensure text isn't rendered in a color that vanishes on a black-and-white printer).
findings.why: This is the one item in my domain's scope with no local evidence that it currently bites: there is no window.print() call anywhere in the app and no user-facing 'print receipt' affordance, so nothing is actively broken. It is flagged at low confidence because a Swiss booking marketplace's confirmation/receipt screens are a plausible, common real-world print target once the product is live, and the absence is currently silent rather than a stated decision.
findings.local_evidence: grep for 'window.print', 'Drucken', 'print receipt' across app/: zero hits, confirming no print feature exists yet to test against.
findings.absence_proof: grep -i 'print style\|@media print\|print:' across _design-system, _rules, _docs, CLAUDE.md: zero hits (only an unrelated 'AGENT_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md: print' referring to console output, and one unrelated TASTE_LOG.md date heading containing the word).
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/SYSTEMS.md or _design-system/SOURCE.md, as a one-line scoped-out note, or _design-system/LOCKFILE.md if the owner decides to build it.
findings.enforcement: doc-only (a decision, not a gate) unless the owner opts to build the feature.
